'''Walter (W.) Dean Harman''' is an American [[chemist]], academic, author and researcher. He is the [[William R. Kenan, Jr.]] Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Virginia]].<ref name=ooa>{{cite web|url=https://chemistry.as.virginia.edu/people/profile/wdh5z|title=W. DEAN HARMAN}}</ref>

Harman's research primarily focuses on [[organic chemistry|organic]], [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic]], and [[organometallic chemistry]]. He has also worked extensively in the area of dearomatization, and has developed new chemical tools based on [[tungsten]], [[osmium]], [[rhenium]], and [[molybdenum]] that are designed to manipulate organic molecules in new ways.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.news.virginia.edu/content/qa-chemistry-department-chair-w-dean-harman/|title=CHEMISTRY CHAIR SEEKS TO 'MAKE A DIFFERENCE' ACROSS THE BOARD|date=7 December 2016}}</ref> He is also the co-author of a textbook for general chemistry with Professor Gordon Yee, entitled ''Thinkwell Chemistry''.

==Early life and education==
Harman is the son of [[Willis Harman]]. He was born on November 4, 1960, in Stanford, California. He studied at [[Stanford University]] and received his bachelor's degree in chemistry in 1983, and a doctoral degree in chemistry in 1987. He then served there as a research associate with [[Henry Taube]] until 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.x-mol.com/university/faculty/1978|title=Harman, W. Dean}}</ref>

==Career==
Harman held a brief appointment as an instructor at Stanford University before joining the University of Virginia as  assistant professor of chemistry in 1989. He was promoted to associate professor in 1994, and became a full professor in the department of chemistry in 1997. He also held an administrative appointment in his career. From 2011 till 2019, he served as the chair of the department of chemistry at the University of Virginia. In 2023, he became the William R. Kenan, Jr. Professor of Chemistry.<ref name=ooa/>

==Research==
Harman specializes in organic, inorganic, and organometallic chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/publications.php?pid=61696&searchstring=&showfilter=all|title=W Dean Harman, Ph.D. - Publications}}</ref> He focuses on the development of a new generation of dearomatization agents based on a matching of the d5/d6 reduction potential of rhenium(I), tungsten(0), and molybdenum(0) complexes with that of pentaammineosmium(II). He is the first to demonstrate the step by step conversion of benzene to cyclohexene with varying degrees of deuterium incorporation while binding to a tungsten complex. He also described the formation of stereoselectively deuterated building blocks for pharmaceutical research.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Preparation of cyclohexene isotopologues and stereoisotopomers from benzene|year=2020|doi=10.1038/s41586-020-2268-y|last1=Smith|first1=Jacob A.|last2=Wilson|first2=Katy B.|last3=Sonstrom|first3=Reilly E.|last4=Kelleher|first4=Patrick J.|last5=Welch|first5=Kevin D.|last6=Pert|first6=Emmit K.|last7=Westendorff|first7=Karl S.|last8=Dickie|first8=Diane A.|last9=Wang|first9=Xiaoping|last10=Pate|first10=Brooks H.|last11=Harman|first11=W. Dean|journal=Nature|volume=581|issue=7808|pages=288–293|pmid=32433618|pmc=7250047|bibcode=2020Natur.581..288S}}</ref>

Harman prepared and explored a series of novel bridgehead CF<sub>3</sub>-substituted isoquinuclidines from decomplexed dihydropyridines, and suggested that dihapto-coordinate complex can be isolated as a single diastereomer, methylated, and reacted with a number of nucleophiles.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jacs.9b10781|title=Molybdenum-Promoted Synthesis of Isoquinuclidines with Bridgehead CF3 Groups|year=2019|doi=10.1021/jacs.9b10781|last1=Wilde|first1=Justin H.|last2=Smith|first2=Jacob A.|last3=Dickie|first3=Diane A.|last4=Harman|first4=W. Dean|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=141|issue=47|pages=18890–18899|pmid=31684729|bibcode=2019JAChS.14118890W |s2cid=207897867 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2017, he reviewed a series of his papers published between 2005 and 2017 that focused on the organic reactions of aromatic ligands η2-coordinated to tungsten, and the usage of these reactions in the synthesis of novel organic substances.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.chemrev.7b00480|title=Group 6 Dihapto-Coordinate Dearomatization Agents for Organic Synthesis|year=2017|doi=10.1021/acs.chemrev.7b00480|last1=Liebov|first1=Benjamin K.|last2=Harman|first2=W. Dean|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=117|issue=22|pages=13721–13755|pmid=29064228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Furthermore, in collaboration with [[Daniel Ess]], he conducted experiments and directed dynamics simulations to investigate η2-arene/aryl hydride equilibria of tungsten benzene complexes in which the arene is held more loosely than in the ground state, primarily through dispersion forces.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Experiments and Direct Dynamics Simulations That Probe η2-Arene/Aryl Hydride Equilibria of Tungsten Benzene Complexes|year=2020|doi=10.1021/jacs.0c08032|last1=Smith|first1=Jacob A.|last2=Schouten|first2=Anna|last3=Wilde|first3=Justin H.|last4=Westendorff|first4=Karl S.|last5=Dickie|first5=Diane A.|last6=Ess|first6=Daniel H.|last7=Harman|first7=W. Dean|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=142|issue=38|pages=16437–16454|pmid=32842728|pmc=7778736|bibcode=2020JAChS.14216437S }}</ref>
